title: Detect Overdue Invoices and Days Late
description:
Identify overdue invoices as of **2024-06-01**. An invoice is overdue if it was paid after its due date (`paid_date > due_date`) or is still unpaid (`paid_date IS NULL`) with a past due date. Return the days overdue for each.

**Table: invoices** — `invoice_id`, `customer_name`, `amount`, `due_date`, `paid_date`

Output columns: `invoice_id`, `customer_name`, `amount`, `due_date`, `days_overdue`. Order by `days_overdue DESC`.
solution_sql: SELECT invoice_id, customer_name, amount, due_date, CASE WHEN paid_date IS NOT NULL THEN (paid_date - due_date) ELSE ('2024-06-01'::DATE - due_date) END AS days_overdue FROM invoices WHERE paid_date > due_date OR (paid_date IS NULL AND due_date < '2024-06-01'::DATE) ORDER BY days_overdue DESC;

test_cases.description: Delta Co (94 days), Gamma Ltd (61 days), Beta Inc (36 days), Zeta Corp (32 days), Eta Inc (29 days) = 5 overdue; ACME paid early, Epsilon paid early, Theta paid early

hints: Use paid_date > due_date OR (paid_date IS NULL AND due_date < '2024-06-01') in the WHERE clause.
For days_overdue: use paid_date - due_date for late-paid invoices; use '2024-06-01' - due_date for still-unpaid ones.
In DuckDB, DATE - DATE returns an INTEGER (number of days), so no special cast is needed.
explanation: ACME paid Mar 25 before due Apr 1 (paid early, not overdue). Beta paid Apr 20 vs due Mar 15 → 36 days late ✓. Gamma unpaid, due Apr 1 → 61 days as of Jun 1 ✓. Delta unpaid, due Feb 28 → 94 days ✓. Epsilon paid May 14 before due May 15 (early). Zeta unpaid, due Apr 30 → 32 days ✓. Eta paid May 30 vs due May 1 → 29 days late ✓. Theta paid Mar 5 before due Mar 10 (early). Five invoices are overdue.
